catalog_fit_tests.reason: Airflow identity is a per-run TaskInstance (dag_id, task_id, run_id, map_index) for a data interval. Catalog unit RES-0063 has no run_id or map_index; inventing map_index=-1 would hide that the native identity is a partitioned/run instance, not the research artifact command-center/research/RES-0063.json.

Prefect task_key is derived from a Python function's last qualname component plus a bytecode hash. The catalog record for RES-0063 is a research question and output path, not a function, so task_key cannot be constructed from catalog fields. DEFAULT cache further binds identity to a flow-run ID the catalog does not have. Wrapping the unit in a @task would identify the wrapper, not command-center/research/RES-0063.json.

Dagster AssetKey is a handle for the asset. Mapping output_path command-center/research/RES-0063.json onto AssetKey(['command-center', 'research', 'RES-0063.json']) uses only catalog fields, invents no partition key, and names the research artifact rather than a data interval. FROM_FAILURE skip of successful materializations matches 'do not redo a delivered unit'.

Flyte Identifier(project, domain, name, version) can be filled from output_path prefix, execution_substrate, id=RES-0063, and sha256(question_or_target). resource_type=TASK is an engine constant. That names a versioned task entity, not the artifact path command-center/research/RES-0063.json; cache keys further include typed inputs. Closer than Airflow's run/map_index, farther than Dagster AssetKey.

subject_unit.question_or_target: How do Airflow, Prefect, Dagster and Flyte define a task's identity, decide what to re-run after a partial failure, and enforce idempotency - and which definition of task identity fits work units whose output is a research artifact rather than a data partition?
subject_unit.title: Extract resume, backfill and idempotency semantics from mature DAG schedulers

task_identity_definitions.idempotency: The engine does not wrap side effects. Idempotency is a task author obligation. Mapped tasks distinguish instances by map_index (a partition of the mapped input), not by output artifact.
task_identity_definitions.identity_statement: A TaskInstance is uniquely constrained as (dag_id, task_id, run_id, map_index); TaskInstance.key also carries try_number. map_index=-1 means unmapped. Docs: a Task Instance is a specific run of that task for a given Dag (and thus for a given data interval).
task_identity_definitions.resume_semantics: Failed TIs enter up_for_retry and are rescheduled; the unique constraint does not include try_number, so a retry is the same identity with an incremented try_number. Succeeded TIs of the same run are not re-created.
task_identity_definitions.title: Airflow TaskInstance composite key

task_identity_definitions.idempotency: Idempotency is opt-in via cache_policy / cache_key_fn and result persistence. DEFAULT cache includes flow-run ID, so the same inputs in a new flow run do not hit cache unless the policy is changed (e.g. INPUTS).
task_identity_definitions.identity_statement: Source: task_key is '{qualname.split('.')[-1]}-{hash(code_obj)}' from _generate_task_key. Docs claim a hash of task name plus the fully qualified name of the function. Those formulas disagree. A task run is a single invocation; DEFAULT cache hashes inputs, code definition, and the prevailing flow-run (or autonomous task-run) ID.
task_identity_definitions.resume_semantics: Retries re-enter Running from Retrying/AwaitingRetry on the same task run. Caching can skip re-execution when a cache key hits.
task_identity_definitions.title: Prefect task_key plus cache key

task_identity_definitions.idempotency: Re-materializing the same unpartitioned AssetKey is the same asset; partitions (when used) are an extra identity axis this program's work units do not carry.
task_identity_definitions.identity_statement: An AssetKey is a handle for referring to the asset: a sanitized string or hierarchical list/tuple of strings. That is artifact identity, not a run-scoped task instance. Op/step retries are a separate axis (RetryPolicy on the computing op).
task_identity_definitions.resume_semantics: Default run retry strategy FROM_FAILURE re-executes from failure: successful ops are skipped and their outputs are reused. FROM_ASSET_FAILURE uses persisted materialization records to exclude already-materialized assets.
task_identity_definitions.title: Dagster AssetKey (asset handle) plus FROM_FAILURE skip

task_identity_definitions.idempotency: Memoization is opt-in (cache=True). Cache identity is the versioned task entity plus typed inputs, not the output artifact path.
task_identity_definitions.identity_statement: Registered tasks are Identifier(resource_type, project, domain, name, version), stringified as '{resource_type_name}:{project}:{domain}:{name}:{version}'. Remote cache keys add Cache Version, Task Signature, and Inputs, isolated by project and domain.
task_identity_definitions.resume_semantics: A cache hit returns the stored result instead of re-running the task. Changing cache_version invalidates prior entries.
task_identity_definitions.title: Flyte Identifier (project, domain, name, version)

which_definition_fits_research_artifact.rationale: Dagster AssetKey names the artifact from output_path with no invented partition. Flyte Identifier can be filled from catalog fields but names a versioned task entity, not the file. Prefect identifies a function/cache key the catalog does not have. Airflow identifies a (run, map_index) instance of a data interval.
